methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Seed → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.5x) to $5M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Chips & Semiconductors (found 0 same-stage, 2 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 13 same-sector peers exist in Chips & Semiconductors, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

methods.name: Public-Comp Anchoring
methods.skip_reason: target revenue not on file (private companies rarely disclose)
methods.rationale: Public Semiconductors P/S median is 18.9x across 3 tickers. Cannot apply without target's revenue.

data.narrative:
Gallox Semiconductors is a Seed-stage chip design company founded by Jon McCandless and Debdeep Jena, having raised $5M+. The sector peer universe spans 3 public comparables (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) and 8 private-stage peers including Cerebras, Credo Semiconductor, and SambaNova Systems.

Stage-progression methodology is the primary applicable valuation anchor. Using total capital raised ($5M) as a proxy for Seed-stage value and applying a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical of Seed-to-next-stage progression yields $12.5M. Peer-median triangulation is not actionable; while 13 same-sector private peers exist, the narrow filters (same stage, adjacent stage, similar tier) return insufficient data points for reliable median extraction. Public-comp anchoring via EV/Revenue multiples is likewise inapplicable—the public Semiconductors median stands at 18.9x P/S across three tickers, but Gallox's revenue is not disclosed, precluding multiplication.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $11M to $14M (median $12M), derived entirely from stage-progression methodology. This narrow single-method result carries material uncertainty. The valuation hinges on the representativeness of the 2.5x multiplier for this target's risk profile and exit potential. Absent revenue data or a sufficient cohort of same-stage comparable exits, external validation remains limited. Key unknowns include product-market fit maturity, IP strength, and management track record in the capital-intensive semiconductor sector.
